name: MO-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+19 partisan lean strongly favors Republicans
Open seat removes any incumbent advantage but does not change the partisan baseline
Democrat Josh Smead has raised only ~$72k with minimal cash on hand
Prediction markets price the Republican at ~95%
model.rationale: This rural northwest Missouri seat carries an R+19 lean, and the Democrat's fundraising is negligible while the Republican nominee has a modest but real financial edge and outside spending on his side. Markets price the race at roughly 95% Republican, so the forecast stays near the fundamentals with no evidence of a competitive race.
model.watch: A late surge in Democratic fundraising or outside spending, or a scandal involving the Republican nominee, would be the main way this moves toward competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Sam Graves (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Sam Graves is retiring from this heavily Republican northwest Missouri district, leaving an open seat that remains strongly tilted toward the GOP. The district's R+19 partisan lean gives Republicans a large structural advantage, and no expert raters list the race as competitive. Prediction markets put the Republican nominee's chances at roughly 95 percent.

Republican Chris Stigall has raised about $600,000 and holds a cash advantage, with some outside spending already opposing him. Democrat Josh Smead has raised only about $72,000 with little cash on hand, and a Libertarian is also on the ballot. With no public polling available, the race rests on fundamentals, all of which point to a Republican hold.
